Design lab · proposal

Card art v1.0-cardart

Six cards redrawn as real pixel art on one 48×48 grid, in two directions, next to the art the game uses today. Approve by code: v1.0-cardart-A (Emblem) or v1.0-cardart-B (Vignette). Nothing in the game changes.

v1.0-cardart-A Emblem

One bold subject centred on a flat night ground. Icon-like, the most readable at 48 px.

v1.0-cardart-B Vignette

A small scene with ground, horizon and light, still one clear subject. More atmosphere, a little less punch at 48 px.

Palette · 17 colours, shared by every picture

Book kit browns, paper and wine, the Spark golds from spark.svg, moss, and a night blue-green family that is also the Collector's mint. Outline is always #2a1d12.

    Compare v1.0-cardart

    Current art: the game's own renderer, at the Deck tile size (44 px inside the 48 px window) and the largest opened size (a 2:3 crop up to 110×165). New art: 1x (Deck and Chain tiles), 2x (opened card), 3x (reward). Rows scroll sideways on a phone.

    In place

    The three looks in a mock of the Deck tile (art at 1x) and the opened card (art at 2x), on the page paper. Note: today's tile window is 48 px outside and 44 px inside; the new art needs 48 px inside (52 outside), drawn here that way.

    Rules for the other 79 cards

    Grid
    48×48 pixels per picture, authored as SVG of whole-pixel squares with shape-rendering="crispEdges". Shown only at 48, 96 or 144 px (1x, 2x, 3x) with image-rendering: pixelated. No painted sources, no gradients, blur, filters or bitmaps.
    Palette
    The 17 colours above and nothing else. Flat fills; light comes from stepped bands of a lighter palette colour, never a blend.
    Outline
    Every subject has a 1 px #2a1d12 outline. Light from the top left: a 1 px pale highlight on the top-left edge, the darker shade on the bottom right, as in the Spark icon.
    Readability
    One subject that says what the card does, about 60 to 70% of the picture. Nothing smaller than 3 px carries meaning. Check every picture at 1x on the paper before it ships.
    Motifs
    Reuse the game's own: the Spark (the approved star, at 16, 11 or 7 px), the wisp (pale orb), the Collector (mint orb), the campfire for Rest, the heart for Save, lanterns, seeds, bells. The same thing is always drawn the same way.
    Rarity changes the picture
    Common: the subject on a plain ground, flat, no light source. Rare: adds a second depth layer behind the subject (a backdrop disc in A, far hills in B) and a light source (a lit rim, the moon, a campfire). Legendary: a richer scene, a stepped glow behind the subject and a 1 px gold key-line inside the frame.
    One picture per card
    No sharing between different cards. An evolved card (II, III) reuses its base picture and adds detail; when it changes rarity, it takes that rarity's layer, light and key-line.
